The user's language (BCP 47): the recognition hint of a capture that names none and the language of the reply

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or fails validation (`validation_failed`).

Conflict.description: The thing is not in a state that allows this (`conflict`, `stale`, `replayed`).

Forbidden.description:
The caller may not do this: `scope_violation` (the path names another session, application or
preparation than the token is bound to), `permission_denied`, `step_up_required` or `quarantined`
(the application's package is not active).

Gone.description: The session has ended; a new session needs a new authenticated context (`expired`).

OAuthFlowNotFound.description: The flow id is unknown or belongs to another principal (`not_found`).

RagNotFound.description:
No such source, or generation, in the caller's scope (`validation_failed`, `details.reason` `not_found`). A
source of another scope is reported exactly like one that does not exist.

Unauthorized.description:
The context token is missing, malformed, expired, replayed or unverifiable (`unauthenticated`,
`expired`, `replayed`, `scope_missing`). Mint a fresh token and retry.

Unavailable.description: A dependency the request needs cannot answer (`unavailable`, `timeout`); nothing was done.

Unprocessable.description: The request is well-formed but its content is refused (for example a package with critical findings).

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The Content-Type is not the one this operation accepts.

ActionFailure.description:
The body of a confirmation that did not commit: the bare Error, or, when an outcome exists, the receipt
beside the Error (ActionOutcome).

status.description:
`cancelling`: the run was in flight and has been told to stop (its own response ends with the cancelled
outcome). `finished`: the run had already ended.

agent.description: The AG-UI `AgentCapabilities` object of the release.

notClaimed.description: Stable identifiers of the features that are not claimed, `voice_full_duplex` among them.

package.description: The release of the AG-UI schemas the events are validated against.

supported_by.description: The task of the plan that makes the feature work.

AguiRunAgentInput.description:
The AG-UI `RunAgentInput` (schemas/agui/ag-ui-core.json, `RunAgentInput`), as far as AlixAI reads it. Everything in it
is data from the client: it is never a capability, a permission, a scope or an instruction.

context.description: The page's readable context. Untrusted, bounded, fenced data that reaches no prompt (until M3-32).

forwardedProps.description: Only the object `alixai` is read: `choiceId` answers the pending clarification, `language` is a BCP 47 tag.

messages.description:
The conversation as the client holds it. The last user message is the utterance and nothing else of it is
read as an instruction; the session store is the record of the conversation. An empty list with no
`resume` is a connect run.

interruptId.description: The preparation id of the interrupt.

payload.description: Exactly `{"approved": true}` or `{"approved": false}` for a resolved interrupt.

runId.description: Identifies the run on its thread; the same id after the run finished returns the recorded run.

state.description:
The client's shared state. An object makes the run update only `/alixai` of it (STATE_DELTA); anything
else makes the first state event a STATE_SNAPSHOT. Untrusted, bounded data.

threadId.description: The session id of the context token.

tools.description: UI declarations of the client. Accepted, never called, never a capability (until M3-32 they are not read further).

health.description: The application's own health report; only read for an active application.

ApplicationEvent.description:
The signed event. Every member that decides what it does is in it, so the signature covers all of it. An
unknown member is refused, never ignored.

application_id.description: Must be the application of the context token.

everything.description: The host cannot say more, so this applies to all pending state of the workspace.

id.description: Identifies the event; deliveries are deduplicated by it.

principal_id.description: Restricts the event to one principal's sessions; required for `principal_change`.

type.description: The host's name for the event ("invoice.paid"): a short label shown in the notice, never interpreted.

signatures.description: Exactly one signature. None is unauthenticated; more than one is `schema_invalid`.

notify_failed.description: Sessions that could not be told. Their state is invalidated all the same.

sessions.description: How many sessions the event changed.

expires_at.description: At most 15 minutes after `signed_at`; the event id is remembered until then.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound of the time of the event.

types.description: Keep only these event types (dotted lower-case names such as `action.committed`).

until.description: Exclusive upper bound of the time of the event. Must be after `since`.

min_confidence.description: Not below `platform_floor`. Left out keeps the current threshold.
The calibrated-confidence floor of the profile; never below `platform_floor`.

mode.description: off disables the layer for the profile; shadow records without using; advisory lets gated results inform interpretation.

allowed_models.description: Provider and model pairs that may receive requests under this level. Empty allows none.

expected_revision.description: The revision the writer read; 0 to create.

files.description: Whether an excerpt of an uploaded file may leave under this level, and up to which class. Absent keeps every excerpt local. Not at source level; internal and confidential need the approval capability.

source_id.description: The RAG source of a source-level policy, and only then.

FileUploadForm.description: The fields of an upload. `treatment` must come before `file`.

Health.description: The members of the readiness report of /readyz, plus the caller's application.

before.description: Delete every transcript turn of the workspace created before this time. Not in the future.

since.description: Include rows created at or after this time.

until.description: Include rows created before this time.

body.description: As `HistoryTurn.body`, an assistant row is sanitised like live text.

withheld.description: Present and true when `body` is empty because the sanitiser refused the text.

snippet.description:
A short excerpt of the row around the match. For a user row it is the user's own words, plain text; for an
assistant row it is sanitised Markdown like `HistoryTurn.body`. Empty if the sanitiser refused it.

next_offset.description: The offset of the next page, or null at the end.

limit.description: How many hits a page holds at most (10 when not given).

offset.description: How many hits to skip; the `next_offset` of the previous page.

session_id.description: Restrict the search to one of the caller's sessions.

text.description:
The words to find; every one must occur in the row. At most 12 distinct words count. Plain text:
nothing in it is syntax.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, or null at the end of the transcript.

total.description: How many rows the session's transcript holds.

act.description: The directive act of an assistant row.

body.description:
A user row: the user's own text, verbatim, plain text. An assistant row: model Markdown sanitised as a
whole exactly as the `token` events of a live turn are (raw HTML and images removed, links limited to the
allowed schemes), so it can be rendered with the renderer used for live text. Empty when `withheld`.

n.description: The turn number inside the session; the user's row and the assistant's row of one turn share it.

withheld.description:
Present and true when `body` is empty because the sanitiser refused the text of an assistant row (the
live stream would have refused it too). History never falls back to the raw text.

redirect_uri.description: The redirect URI the browser arrived on, without the query.

callback.description: Who receives the provider redirect. Default host. loopback: AlixAI binds 127.0.0.1 and completes the exchange; redirect_uri must still be the documented placeholder.

capabilities.description: The capabilities to connect for; the engine requests the smallest set of provider scopes they map to.

opener_origin.description:
Exact origin of the host page that opened the popup (scheme://host[:port], no path, query or fragment).
Required when presentation is popup; used only as postMessage targetOrigin. Validated against the operator allowlist
`external_providers.oauth.popup_origins` (never `*`). Ignored for presentation redirect.

reauthorize.description: An existing connection to renew (re-consent or account switch).

redirect_uri.description:
Where the provider sends the browser back. Bound to the flow and checked again at the callback when `callback` is `host`.
Remains required for wire compatibility with 1.0 (dropping a required member is a breaking change under tools/compat).
When `callback` is `loopback`, send the placeholder `http://127.0.0.1/oauth/loopback`; AlixAI ignores it and uses the ephemeral listener it bound.

account.description: The known account when re-authorizing, otherwise null members (the user picks it at the provider).

flow_id.description: Opaque id of the flow. Present when presentation is popup so the opener can poll; optional for additive compatibility with 1.0 responses.

poll_interval_ms.description: Suggested polling interval for GET /v1/oauth/flows/{flow_id}. Present with flow_id when presentation is popup.

kind.description: confirmation (a prepared action awaits the user), clarification (a question awaits an answer) or goal.

ProviderCredentialSubmit.description: The secret is in `key`. It is write-only.

key.description: The API key or token. Never returned, logged or put in an error.

scopes.description: The provider scopes the capability needs; the validation probe asks for no more.

reason.description: A fixed code, never free text.

decided_by.description: The level that set the effective mode, `default` or `kill_switch`.

levels.description: The mode of each level that has a setting.

behavior.description: What the service does instead, set when the role is not `ok` (master plan 18).

configured.description: Whether a provider is registered for the role.

effect.description: The stable degradation code, set when the role is not `ok`.

provider.description: The runtime that serves the role ("localai", "fake"), when it names itself.

reason.description: A short explanation when the role is not `ok` (redacted).

version.description: The runtime version the adapter observed.

max_depth.description: The configured limit on pending jobs of the class.

oldest_ready_age_ms.description:
How long the longest-waiting ready job has been eligible to run. Only the deployment-wide view knows
it, so it is absent here.

pending.description: Waiting jobs, including retries still in back-off.

priority.description: The rank of the class, 1 the most urgent.

workers.description: The configured workers of the class.

classes.description: All six classes, most urgent first.

RagCitationResolution.description: What the reference of a citation resolves to, read at the moment it is resolved.

availability.description: Whether the source can be opened now, not at retrieval.

locator.description: Where in the source the cited passage sits, when known.

The way to open the source itself: the host's own record or file reference when the source has one, else
the source resolved by id. Opaque, never a URL or a path.

staleness.description: Whether the cited version is the latest, now.

version.description: The source version or content hash the citation was grounded on.

checked.description: Registrations of the scope that were looked at.

True while the source is bound to the application's active package and may be read. A source registered
under a package that was replaced is false until it is re-bound, and so is one whose removal began.

What a caller may say when it registers a source: the name the application's active package declares it under.
The object is closed; nothing else (a root, a path, a tenant, a workspace) can be named.

declaration.description: The name the active package declares the source under.

findings.description: Warnings and information from the load checks. A package with a critical finding is refused.

seq.description:
Numbers the announcements of one session from a time-based value (the Unix time in seconds when the
session's feed began) and only increases; the SSE `id` and the resume cursor.

outcome.description: What the report permits. Present when audited.

extra_confirmation.description: True when requires_confirmation is true only because settings asked for it.

fields.description: The fields the caller may supply, in declaration order.

requires_confirmation.description: A commit needs an explicit confirmation (the platform floor and host policy, plus any extra confirmation settings asked for).

requires_step_up.description: A commit needs the host application's own step-up.

risk_level.description: The effective risk level the policy gateway assigns (0 read, 1 reversible, 2 consequential, 3 privileged).

default.description: The profile in force when no level states one.

selected.description: The profile the caller's effective settings select.

status.description: The worst status of any role.

SettingsProviderRole.description: One model role. It names no runtime, address, version or free-text reason.

effect.description: The stable degradation code when status is not ok.

SettingsTenantRecord.description: The tenant settings document of the caller's tenant with its revision.

SettingsUserRecord.description: The user settings document of the caller with its revision.

version.description: 0 when the level has no document yet, otherwise 1 for the first write and one more for every change.

SettingsUserUpdate.description: The request body of PUT /v1/settings/user. Nothing else is accepted; the key of the document comes from the token.

expected_version.description: The version that was read, or 0 to create the document.

TurnRequest.description: Exactly one of text, choice_id, confirmation and reject; attachments only with text.

attachments.description:
The files the user attached to this message: ids of `POST /v1/files`, at most 4, each resolved under the
turn's scope (see the description of the operation). Only a turn with `text` carries them; a file named
twice counts once.

choice_id.description: Selects one of the choices of the pending clarification.

token.description: The single-use confirmation secret that came with the prepared action.

language.description: A BCP 47 tag the core supports ("en", "it"); empty lets the core choose.

text.description: The user's message (or a finalised transcript).

confirmation.description: Present when the turn prepared an action that needs the user's explicit confirmation.

bearerAuth.description:
A single-use application context token (ADR 0013): a JWS signed with the host application's Ed25519
key (`alg` EdDSA, `typ` alixai-context+jwt) carrying application_id, tenant_id, workspace_id, `sub`
(the principal), roles, capability_scopes and session_id. Sent only in the Authorization header,
never in a query string, a cookie or a body.

info.description:
AlixAI is a headless, application-bound assistant core. A host application authenticates its user,
exchanges that identity for a short-lived context token (ADR 0013) and calls this API with it.

**Identity.** Every route below `/v1` needs `Authorization: Bearer <context token>`. The token carries
the application, tenant, workspace, principal, roles, capability scopes and session; nothing about
them is read from a path, a query or a body. A token is **single use**: every request, and every
event-stream open, needs a fresh one; a second presentation is `replayed`. The deployment level of
the scope is configuration and is never reported.

**Errors.** Every failure is the bare `Error` document (`code`, `message`, `retryable`, `details`),
whatever the status. The one exception is a confirmation whose commit reached the host and did not
succeed (`confirmAction`, 409 and 500): the receipt, the durable record of what happened, comes beside
the `Error`. The request id is in the `X-Request-ID` response header and in `details.request_id`.

**Quarantine.** An application whose package is not active (quarantined, rejected, superseded or not
installed) serves no traffic: its sessions, turns, actions and capabilities answer `quarantined`.
Registering a package only ever installs it into quarantine.

**Streaming.** A turn answers with TurnEvents (schemas/conversation/turn-event). Ask for
`text/event-stream` to receive them as server-sent events; `id` is the event's `seq`, `event` its `type`
and `data` the TurnEvent JSON on one line. A dropped connection resumes from the last `id` seen with
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}/events` (header `Last-Event-ID` or query `cursor`); the turn is
never run again. LocalAI's own endpoints are never exposed.

**How this document is assembled.** This root lists one fragment per area under `paths/` in
`x-alixai-areas`. A fragment is a mapping with an optional `paths` (path items) and an optional
`components` (schemas, responses, parameters). A task that adds endpoints fills its own fragment and
never edits this file; `TestRoutesMatchOpenAPISpec` fails when a registered route is missing from the
merged document, or an operation in it has no route.

get.summary: Liveness

get.description:
200 when the service can answer (the controller role is usable and every check passes), 503 when it
cannot. A degraded service (a missing router or embedder) is still ready. The report is cached for
gateway.health_ttl so an anonymous caller cannot turn it into load on the runtime.

get.description:
The prepared action with its current state. A preparation of another tenant, workspace, principal or
session is `scope_violation`, the same as one that does not exist.
get.summary: Inspect a preparation

post.description:
Presents the single-use confirmation secret and, if it is the right one for this preparation, principal,
session and set of data versions, commits the action through the coordinator. The secret is used up by
the first presentation: the second is `replayed` (409) and reaches no adapter. A level 3 action cannot be
confirmed here (`step_up_required`, 403). Preparations expire after at most ten minutes (`expired`).

200 carries the receipt of a committed or queued outcome. A rejected outcome (the host refused, nothing was
applied) is 409 and a partial or uncertain one is 500, each with the same body shape plus `error`: the
receipt is the durable record, `error` says why. An uncertain outcome is never retried by the core; read
the receipt later.

200.description: The action was committed (or queued); the receipt says which.

409.description:
Not committed. Either the confirmation or the preparation is not in a state that allows it
(`replayed`, `conflict`, `stale`: the bare `Error`), or the host refused the commit and nothing was
applied (the receipt, status `rejected`, beside the `Error` that carries the host's reason).

500.description:
The outcome is partial or unknown (`partial_failure`, `uncertain_outcome`: the receipt beside the
`Error`), or the commit failed internally (the bare `Error`).

post.summary: Present the confirmation and commit the action

get.description: The durable outcome. `conflict` while the preparation has no outcome yet.
get.summary: Retrieve the receipt of an action

post.description: Nothing is sent to the application. Rejecting a rejected preparation returns it.

The body is the AG-UI `RunAgentInput`. Members this API does not read (`parentRunId`, members of a newer
protocol version, `forwardedProps` beyond the `alixai` object) are accepted and ignored. Exactly one thing is
answered:

- the last message when its role is `user`: the text (and the pre-uploaded files it names, as `file` content
  parts whose `source` is `{type: "file", value: <file id of POST /v1/files>}`; inline bytes and URLs are
  refused), as a turn of the dialogue engine;
- `forwardedProps.alixai.choiceId`: the choice of the pending clarification, with no model involved;
- `resume`: the answer to an interrupt, `[{interruptId: <preparation id>, status: "resolved", payload:
  {"approved": true | false}}]` (status `cancelled` declines). Only an explicit `{"approved": true}`
  approves, and an approval carries the confirmation secret in the `X-AlixAI-Confirmation-Token` request
  header, never in the body. The same answer in the form of a tool message for the call
  `alixai_confirm_<preparation id>` is accepted;
- no messages and no resume: a **connect** run, which replays the thread's history and state and runs no
  turn (it needs the host to have put `history.read` in the context token).

`threadId` must be the session id of the context token. Any other thread, an interrupt of another thread, of
another principal or tenant and one that never existed are one and the same `403 scope_violation`.

**Events.** Server-sent events: each event is `data: <AG-UI event on one line>` followed by a blank line;
`id: <seq>` (the seq of the TurnEvent the events were produced for, the resume cursor) is on the LAST event
of each TurnEvent, so a client that lost the connection and sends the last id it received always resumes at a
TurnEvent boundary. The run ends with `RUN_FINISHED` (outcome `success`, `interrupt` or `cancelled`) or
`RUN_ERROR`. A prepared action ends the run with an interrupt outcome; resume it with a new run.

**The confirmation secret** of the action a run prepared is the `X-AlixAI-Confirmation-Token` response header,
sent only when the run's account was shown in full and ended in its interrupt. It is in no event and no body.
The host backend's SDK agent keeps it per thread and preparation and sends it back on the resume; the browser
never holds it. A retry of the run and every reconnect replay the events and never send the secret again.

**Retry.** A run is identified by `(threadId, runId)`. The same `runId` after the run has finished returns
the recorded run (the buffered events, from the start) and never runs a second turn; while the first request is
still running it is `409 conflict` (`details.reason: run_in_progress`). A new `runId` is a new turn.

A sequence of `data: <AG-UI event JSON>` frames, with `id: <seq>` on the last event of each TurnEvent;

interrupt that asks for the confirmation. Sent to the host backend's SDK agent only.

The AG-UI protocol version and release implemented, the event types emitted and not emitted, the AG-UI
`AgentCapabilities` object, the identifiers of the features that are not claimed (`notClaimed`: reasoning,
sub-agents, Raw events, chunk forms, predictive state updates, inline attachments, model-generated suggestions,
full duplex voice, and, until the task that implements them, client tools and client context) and the

get.summary: What the AG-UI endpoint claims

post.description:
Cancels the request that runs the turn: the engine stops, no confirmation is presented and nothing is
committed. The response of the run's own request then ends with `RUN_FINISHED` and the `cancelled` outcome.
A run that is a resume was already confirmed by the user, and a commit that has begun is not undone: cancel
leaves nothing committed unless the user had already confirmed. A run that has already finished has nothing
to stop (`finished`): the receipt it has stands, and a prepared action it left pending is declined by a
resume with status `cancelled`. A run that is not the caller's, or does not exist, is the same `403` as for
the events route.
post.summary: Stop a run that is still in flight

get.description:
The events of a run the caller made, mapped again from the buffered TurnEvents of the stream hub, so that a
client that lost its connection continues without the turn being run again: this route only reads. The
mapping is a pure function of the run's context and the buffered TurnEvents, so the events are byte for byte
those the run sent, and the confirmation secret is never sent again.

**Transport.** Server-sent events by default (`data: <event>` lines, `id: <seq>` on the last event of each
TurnEvent). A request with `Upgrade: websocket` is served as a WebSocket: one text message per event, exactly
the data line of the SSE event, server to client only (a message from the client closes the connection),
subprotocol `alixai.agui.v1`, a normal closure (1000) after the last event. The socket carries no ids, so a
WebSocket reader that must resume passes the `cursor` it learned over SSE, or starts again from the beginning.
A browser's `Origin` must be the request's own host: no CORS header is ever sent.

**Resume.** The cursor is the `seq` of the last TurnEvent the client has (`Last-Event-ID` or `cursor`; the
later wins); the response is the events after it. No cursor is the start. A malformed cursor, or one ahead
of the stream, is `400`; one behind the retained window is `410`; one at the end of a finished run is `204`
(stop reconnecting). A run that does not exist, one of another principal and one past its retention are the
same `403` (`scope_violation`, `details.reason: turn_not_visible`); a run whose first request is still
running is `409 conflict`. A context token is single use: every reconnect needs a fresh one.

101.description: The connection is upgraded to a WebSocket (the request carried `Upgrade: websocket`).

text/event-stream.description: One server-sent event per AG-UI event.

200.description: The events of the run after the cursor.

204.description: The cursor is at the end of a finished run: the client has every event. Stop reconnecting.

get.summary: Read the events of a run again, from a cursor

post.description:
The body is a signed `.tar.gz` application package (docs/integration/application-package.md), sent as
`application/gzip`. The token must carry the capability scope `applications.register` and the package
must declare the token's application: a token for application A can never install a package of B. The
package must be signed by a publisher key the operator registered, have no critical finding and be
compatible with this core; otherwise it is refused (422) and nothing is written. The size is limited by
gateway.max_body_bytes.

201 when the package was installed, 200 when the very same content was already installed (its state is
returned as it is: registering again never resets a state). The record is `quarantined`.
post.summary: Register an application package (it lands in quarantine)

get.description:
The installed packages of the token's application with their states, and the application's own health
for an active one. Any other application id is `scope_violation`, whether or not it exists.
get.summary: Inspect the caller's application

get.description:
The capabilities of the application's active package that the policy gateway exposes to this token (scope,
roles, host rules), with the effective risk level and what a commit needs. It is the same exposure the
model gets. An application whose package is not active answers `quarantined`.
get.summary: List the capabilities the caller may see

get.description:
The configuration of every approved profile of the caller's application, and the platform floor under which no
threshold is ever accepted. Operator only: `permission_denied` for everybody else.
get.summary: Read the decision-layer configuration (operator only)

put.description:
Sets the `mode` of one profile (`off` disables the layer for it) and, when given, its `min_confidence`
threshold. A threshold below `platform_floor` is `validation_failed` with `details.reason`
`below_platform_floor` and nothing is changed; leaving it out keeps the profile's current threshold. A profile
the deployment does not approve is `validation_failed`. The change is audited. Operator only: `permission_denied`
for everybody else, before the body is read.

200.description: The profile as it now stands.

put.summary: Enable, shadow or disable one profile and set its threshold (operator only)

get.description:
Which decision provider and model are configured, in what mode (`off`, `shadow` or `advisory`), how often the
layer fell back and why, and how many results were accepted and rejected since the counters started, for the
caller's own application and tenant. Advisory aggregate state only: never an authorisation, a score or a
commit result. Needs `decision.status.read`.
get.summary: Decision-layer status of the caller's own scope

get.description:
Reports whether record-to-text is available for the token's scope, whether recognition is local or external,
the maximum clip length, and the only accepted audio shape (WAV, PCM s16le, mono, 16000 Hz). The host uses
this to show or hide the record control. Scoped like every other `/v1` route. A deployment with no STT
answers with `available` false and `locality` `none` (or `503 unavailable` when the transcription service
is not wired at all).
get.summary: Dictation capabilities of this deployment

post.description:
The host application tells AlixAI that something changed, so that state AlixAI holds about it is
invalidated and the sessions it concerns are told. The body is the delivery of the event adapter
(adapters/events): the event and exactly ONE detached Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of
the event as received, by a key registered for the application. A delivery with no signature is
`unauthenticated`, with several `schema_invalid`; a signature valid for more than 15 minutes is refused. The
body is at most 64 KiB.

**What authenticates and scopes it.** The request carries a context token like every `/v1` request, and the
token's application is the one thing taken from it: it picks the application whose keys are tried (an
application whose package is not active serves nothing, `quarantined`). The signature authenticates the event.
The tenant and workspace an event is about, and so the sessions it reaches, come ONLY from the signed
payload: the token's own tenant, workspace, principal and session, the URL, the query and the headers never
name or widen a scope. An event for another application than the token's is `scope_violation` even when its
signature is genuine.

**Replay.** The event `id` is remembered until its signature expires; a second delivery of the same event is
acknowledged with `status: duplicate` and changes nothing, whatever signature it carries.

**What the sessions see.** Each session the event changed is told with a notice (a failed turn of two events:
a `stale` error that says nothing was committed, and `done` failed) and an announcement on
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events`. A `5xx`/`503` means the event was not applied (or not recorded) and
should be delivered again: applying is idempotent.

200.description: The event was applied, or had already been applied.

post.description:
Stores one file for the caller and returns its reference. The request is `multipart/form-data` with an
optional `treatment` field, which must come before the file, and exactly one `file` part. The part's
`Content-Type` is the media type the sender declares; it must be one the host's attachment policy allows
and it must be what the bytes are (the core sniffs them), or nothing is stored (`validation_failed`, with
`details.reason` `mime_mismatch`, `mime_not_allowed`, `mime_declared`, `empty` or `too_large`). HTML, SVG, XML
and script types are never stored.

How the file is treated is the host's declared attachment policy: ephemeral turn context, an explicitly
registered RAG source or an application object. Without a `treatment` the policy's default applies; one the
policy does not accept is `permission_denied` (`details.reason` `treatment_not_allowed`). The default is
`ephemeral_context`: readable by the model and previewable by its uploader, inside the session that
uploaded it, for a short time.

The size is bounded by the policy, by the deployment's attachment ceiling (`settings.max_attachment_mb`) and
by `files.max_file_bytes`. The request body has a limit of its own, not the gateway's `max_body_bytes`
(64 KiB by default, which every other route keeps): `files.max_file_bytes` plus a fixed allowance for the
multipart framing, never above the gateway's 16 MiB ceiling. It applies before this operation runs: a
declared `Content-Length` over it is a 413 before a byte of the body is read, and a body that goes over
it is cut off (413). A tenant has a quota of live files and bytes, across its workspaces (507).

file.contentType: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain, text/markdown, text/csv, application/json

Location.description: The path of the new reference.

507.description:
The tenant is over its quota of live files or bytes (`resource_exhausted`, `details.reason`
`quota_files` or `quota_bytes`). Deleting a file frees its room at once.

delete.description:
Only the owner can delete a file. The reference stops resolving at once; the bytes are removed by background
compaction once no other reference of the same scope uses them. A file registered as a RAG source is withdrawn
from the RAG pipeline first; if that fails the file stays and the call fails (`unavailable`).

get.description:
The reference as the caller holds it: size, media type, owner, origin, treatment, permissions, whether it
can be previewed and when it expires. A reference of another scope, another principal's private file, a
file of another session's ephemeral context and a deleted file are all `scope_violation`.

410.description: The reference has expired (`expired`). It is no longer resolvable and its bytes are removed in the background.

get.summary: Read a file reference

get.description:
The file's bytes, always as an attachment (`Content-Disposition: attachment`), with the sniffed media type,
`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a `Content-Security-Policy` that sandboxes everything, so it can never
run in the browser that fetches it. Needs the `download` permission, which the host's policy grants per
treatment (an ephemeral context does not have it by default: `permission_denied`).
get.summary: Download a file

get.description:
A safe rendering, for the types that have a safe previewer: raster images (served as themselves) and text
(served as `text/plain`, cut to `files.preview_text_bytes`; `X-Alixai-Preview-Truncated: true` says it was).
PDF, Office files and anything scriptable have none (`415`, `details.reason` `not_previewable`). Served inline
with `nosniff` and a sandboxing `Content-Security-Policy`. Needs the `preview` permission.

X-Alixai-Preview-Truncated.description: `true` when a text preview was cut to its limit.

415.description: There is no safe previewer for this file type (`validation_failed`, `details.reason` `not_previewable`).

get.summary: Preview a file

get.description: The readiness report of /readyz plus the state of the caller's application.
get.summary: Authenticated health

post.description:
Deletes every transcript turn of the token's WORKSPACE (all its principals and sessions) created before
`before`, and returns how many rows went. It reaches beyond the caller's own history, so it needs its own
capability, `history.cleanup`, which the host should grant only to whoever manages history; the caller is
authorised before anything is deleted. `before` cannot be in the future. Like clearing a session it leaves
the session state, receipts, audit events, records and sources alone, and it is recorded in the audit log
first. The retention policy of the application and tenant is applied by a scheduled job, not by this call.

200.description: The history before the cutoff is deleted.

post.summary: Delete the workspace's history older than a time

post.description:
Streams the caller's own transcript as JSON lines (`application/x-ndjson`): one `HistoryExportRow` per
line, oldest first, then a last line, a `HistoryExportTrailer` `{"complete": true, "rows": N}`. The
status is sent before the rows, so a failure half way cannot change it: an export is whole only if it ends
with the trailer. The export is recorded in the audit log before the first row is sent, and refused if it
cannot be recorded. The body is optional; `session_id` restricts the export to one of the caller's
sessions, `since` (inclusive) and `until` (exclusive) bound the creation time. Needs `history.export`.

schema.description: Lines of JSON, each a `HistoryExportRow` except the last, which is a `HistoryExportTrailer`.

post.description:
Full-text search over the caller's own transcript rows, in every session of the token's workspace. Every
word of `text` must occur in the row; the words are plain text (an operator, a quote, a star or a column
name is just a word or a separator), matched without regard to case or accents. Best match first.
Another principal's rows, and everything of another tenant, workspace or application, never appear. The
text is sent in the body, never in the URL, because a URL is logged. Needs `history.search`.

delete.description:
Deletes the transcript of the session and returns how many rows went; clearing a session with no transcript
deletes nothing and is not an error. Only the transcript goes (and, with it, its search index entries):
the session itself, its prepared actions, receipts and audit events are not touched. The deletion is
recorded in the audit log first and is refused if it cannot be recorded. The session id must be the
token's session and the transcript the caller's own. Needs `history.clear`.
delete.summary: Clear the transcript of the session

get.description:
A page of the session's transcript: whole turns, oldest first. A turn is the user's row and the assistant's
row that share a turn number `n` (a turn can have just one of them), and a page never splits a turn, so
continuing from `next_cursor` can neither skip nor repeat a row. `limit` counts turns. `next_cursor` is
null on the last page. The session id must be the token's session and the transcript the caller's own.
A session with no transcript is an empty page. Needs `history.read`.
get.summary: Read a page of the transcript

post.description: Passes the redirect the browser followed to the OAuth engine, with the token's scope (which must be the scope that started the flow, principal included). A state that is unknown, replayed, expired or issued to another scope is refused and spent; nothing is stored unless every check passed. The code and the state are never echoed or logged. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read. Used by the host-callback path; a loopback popup flow completes inside AlixAI and does not call this route.

200.description: The connection status of the new connection.

delete.description: Cancels a pending flow (the user closed the popup). Idempotent: a flow that is already completed, failed, expired or cancelled answers `204` without changing a finished outcome. Only the principal that started the flow may cancel it; any other caller answers `not_found`. Operator only.

204.description: The flow is cancelled, or was already terminal.

delete.summary: Cancel a pending popup OAuth flow

get.description: Returns the server-side status of a flow started with `presentation` `popup`. Only the principal that started the flow may read it (same application, tenant, workspace and principal); any other caller, and an unknown id, answers `not_found`. Operator only. This is the source of truth when `window.opener` is nulled.
get.summary: Read the status of a popup OAuth flow

parameters.description: The opaque flow id returned by start when presentation is popup.
parameters.name: flow_id

post.description:
Prepares the consent for the requested capabilities (the smallest set of provider scopes they map to) and begins the authorization. A provider without OAuth for API access answers `validation_failed` with `details.reason` `manual_fallback`: use the manual credential route. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

**Presentation.** `presentation` defaults to `redirect` (1.0 behaviour: the host navigates or opens a full window and relays the callback). `popup` keeps the host page in place: the response includes `flow_id` and `poll_interval_ms` so the opener can poll `GET /v1/oauth/flows/{flow_id}`. With `popup`, `opener_origin` is required: the exact origin (scheme://host[:port], no path) of the host page, used only as the `targetOrigin` of the callback page's postMessage. It is validated against the operator allowlist `external_providers.oauth.popup_origins` (never `*`).

**Callback.** `callback` defaults to `host` (the host's registered `redirect_uri` receives the provider redirect). `loopback` means AlixAI binds an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 listener and completes the exchange itself; the caller still sends `redirect_uri` (required for wire compatibility) with the placeholder `http://127.0.0.1/oauth/loopback`.

parameters.description: The provider id (for example `openai`, `openrouter`, `xai`, `moonshot`, `deepgram`, `elevenlabs`, `google-stt`). Slug pattern; not an enum.
parameters.name: provider

200.description: The authorization URL and the consent to show.

post.summary: Start the OAuth authorization of a provider

post.description:
Streams the audit events of the caller's own application, tenant and workspace as JSON lines
(`application/x-ndjson`), oldest first: one audit event per line exactly as stored (already redacted, and
verifiable against its hash), then a last line, an `AuditExportTrailer` `{"complete": true, "events": N}`.
The status is sent with the first byte, so a refusal is an ordinary error response and nothing is sent; a
failure half way is told by the missing trailer. The export is itself recorded in the audit log before the
first event is read, and refused if it cannot be recorded. The body is optional; `types` keeps only those
event types, `since` (inclusive) and `until` (exclusive) bound the time of the event. Needs `audit.export`.

schema.description: Lines of JSON, each an audit event except the last, which is an `AuditExportTrailer`.

post.summary: Export the caller's own audit events

get.description:
The model roles (controller, router, embedder, reranker and the voice roles): whether a provider is
configured for each, which runtime and version serve it, its health and, when it is not `ok`, the stable
degradation code and what the service does instead (master plan 18). `status` is the summary: `unavailable`
when the controller cannot answer, `degraded` when any other configured role is not `ok`. Reasons are
redacted. Needs `ops.providers.read`.
get.summary: Provider and model status

get.description:
The job queue as the caller's own application, tenant and workspace see it: for each of the six priority
classes (master plan 17.1, most urgent first) the configured workers and depth limit and the number of jobs
pending, running, succeeded, failed and cancelled. Succeeded, failed and cancelled count the finished jobs
still retained. Other applications, tenants and workspaces are never counted. Needs `ops.queue.read`.
get.summary: Queue status of the caller's own scope

get.description: The provider profiles of the caller's application with the connection status of the caller's tenant: the state, how it is connected (`oauth` or `api_key`), a safe account identifier, times, warnings, health, budget state and whether the billing notice was acknowledged. Never a credential reference, a fingerprint or a secret. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.
get.summary: List provider profiles and their connection status

get.description: Per-provider, tenant, workspace and principal budgets (integer micro-units) with their current state: spent, remaining, warnings and hard stops. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

200.description: The budgets of the scope with the state of each.

get.summary: Budgets and their states

put.description: An empty `budget_id` creates a budget; a given one must carry its current `revision`. A provider-wide budget needs a deployment operator; a tenant, workspace or principal budget needs a tenant administrator. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

get.description: The data-egress policy (what may leave) at one level of the caller's scope. A level with no policy is disabled. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

parameters.description: The RAG source of a source-level policy, and only then.
parameters.name: source_id

200.description: The policy, or null when the level has none (external processing is disabled there).

get.summary: Read the egress policy of one level

put.description: Creates or replaces the policy of one level. The tenant, workspace and source levels need a tenant administrator; the application and deployment levels need a deployment operator. The token must also carry the policy capability of the level (`dataegress.<level>.write`, and `dataegress.approve` for a policy that lets internal data leave). A stale `expected_revision` is `conflict`. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.
put.summary: Create or replace the egress policy of one level

get.description: Whether the global external-disable switch is engaged. A deployment operator only (`permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read).
get.summary: Read the global kill switch

put.description: Engaging stops every external provider request of the deployment at once, whatever any policy says, and survives a restart. Releasing it enables nothing by itself. The change is audited with the operator and a fixed reason code. A deployment operator only (`permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read).
put.summary: Engage or release the global kill switch

get.description: The mode configured at each level (deployment, application, tenant), the effective mode (the most restrictive level; `local` under the kill switch) and what decided it. Local is the default everywhere. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.
get.summary: Read the mode of the caller's scope

put.description: Sets `local`, `hybrid` or `external` at one level of the caller's own scope. The tenant level needs a tenant administrator; the application and deployment levels need a deployment operator. The change is audited with the operator, the level and the previous and new mode. The M3 settings API cannot do this. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.
put.summary: Set the mode of one level

get.description: The usage records (no prompt and no response) with totals per provider, channel and currency, for reconciliation with the provider's invoice. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

parameters.description: The tenant (default) or the whole application (a deployment operator).
parameters.name: scope

200.description: The usage records with totals, as JSON or CSV.

get.summary: Export usage

post.description: Records that the operator has seen the provider's billing notice (a consumer chat subscription is not API access; API usage is billed separately) and confirms both statements. The operator and the time are the token's and the clock's. The notice version must be the profile's current one. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

delete.description: Revokes the tenant's credential for the provider immediately. Calls that need it fail closed and never fall back by themselves. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

200.description: The connection status after the credential was revoked (revocation at the provider is attempted first where the provider offers it).

put.description: The one place a secret enters the system over HTTP, for providers without a suitable OAuth flow. The key goes straight to the credential service, is validated with a minimally scoped provider request and stored in the secret backend; it is never returned, logged or put in an error (every failure carries a fixed message). The connection status afterwards shows only the state and a safe account identifier. A key the provider reports as broader than needed is stored quarantined. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

200.description: The connection status. The value is never returned.

get.description: Which provider and model would process a request, which data classes and categories may leave, whether RAG excerpts are included, the provider's stated retention and training terms, an upper-bound cost and what happens when the provider is unavailable. When any request-independent check fails (kill switch, policy, profile, allowlist, region) nothing is listed as leaving. It records nothing. Operator only (a tenant administrator of the deployment's own configuration unless said otherwise); `permission_denied` for everybody else, before the body is read.

parameters.description: The model role the request is for; default `conversational_controller`.
parameters.name: role

parameters.description: A RAG source the request would draw on; repeatable.
parameters.name: source

get.summary: Egress disclosure

post.description:
A grounded answer: the claims, each tied to the citations that support it, and the citations themselves, one per
original source, with its authorised name, version, location, availability, staleness and a permission-checked
open reference. If no authorised evidence supports an answer the result is the typed `no_supported_evidence`
outcome (a 200), with a reason; the model's own knowledge is never turned into an uncited answer. A request that
could not run (the model or the source store unavailable, a timeout) is a typed error and never a
`no_supported_evidence` result. Mounted only when the deployment provides the retrieval service.

The open reference of a citation is resolved with `GET /v1/rag/citations/{file_id}`; it is held in memory, valid
for `rag_answer.ref_ttl` (15 minutes by default) and invalid after a restart.

200.description: The answer or the typed absence of one.

502.description: The model's output could not be used (`schema_invalid`); nothing is returned.

504.description: The answer ran out of time (`timeout`); nothing is returned.

get.description:
What the `file` open reference of a citation resolves to, read now: the source's name, version, location and
state, the passage that was cited and the way to open the source itself (the host's own record or file reference,
or the source resolved by id). The reference is bound to the application, tenant, workspace and principal the
answer was written for; resolving it checks the scope, then the expiry, then asks the source catalog, fresh,
whether the principal may still read the source. Every reference that does not resolve for the caller (unknown,
another scope's, a source no longer readable) is one and the same `permission_denied`, so a reference cannot be
used to probe for sources. An expired reference is `expired` (410). Never served by the files service.

410.description: The reference has expired (`expired`). Ask the question again for a new one.

get.summary: Resolve the reference of a citation

post.description:
Passages of the sources the principal may read, best first, each with its source, version, location, state, a
permission-checked open reference and the matching text. The body can only narrow a search (`source_ids` is
intersected with the authorised sources and an id outside them is dropped without saying whether it exists).
An empty `results` is a successful search that matched nothing; it is not an answer and not an error. A search
that could not run is a typed error (`unavailable`, `timeout`), never an empty result. `notices` label a degraded
search, for example `reduced_semantic_recall` when only full-text search ran. Mounted only when the deployment
provides the retrieval service.

504.description: The search ran out of time (`timeout`); nothing is returned.

get.description:
Every source registered for the verified tenant and workspace, ordered by id, with its status. A source of
another tenant or workspace is never listed. Needs nothing but the verified scope.
get.summary: List the sources of the caller's scope

post.description:
Registers the source the application's active package declares under `declaration`, for the verified tenant
and workspace, and has ingestion compare it with what was last scanned (queueing a sync when it is new or its
rules changed). Idempotent per scope and declaration: registering it again returns the existing registration,
re-bound to the active package. Needs the operator action `manage_sources`.

A name the package does not declare is `validation_failed` with `details.reason` `not_declared`. A source
whose removal began is `conflict` until the removal is finished (remove it again). A registration read back
after a restart is not served until the process has re-bound it to the package; until then the answer is a
retryable `unavailable` (503), not `not_found`.
post.summary: Register a source the package declares

post.description:
Updates the registrations of the verified scope after the package was replaced or re-audited: each source is
rebuilt from the package and ingestion rescans it when its rules changed. A source the package no longer
declares is removed, with its declared deletion behaviour. It touches the caller's scope only. Needs the
operator action `manage_sources`. The body is empty or `{}`.
post.summary: Re-bind the caller's sources to the active package

delete.description:
The source stops being served at once and ingestion applies its declared deletion behaviour (audited). If that
fails the source stays unserved and the call can be repeated. Needs the operator action `manage_sources`.

get.description:
The source with its status: lifecycle state, availability, staleness, when the last sync attempt started and
when one really completed, the counts by outcome and the index generation that serves it. This is how
indexing is monitored. A source of another scope is reported exactly like one that does not exist
(`not_found`). Needs nothing but the verified scope.
get.summary: Inspect a source and its indexing status

get.description:
The generations of the source, newest first, each with the component versions it was built with, its counts and
its lifecycle times. A generation is `active` (at most one), `building`, `validating`, `superseded` (kept for
rollback), `failed` or `invalidated`. Needs nothing but the verified scope. Mounted only when the deployment
provides the indexing service.
get.summary: List the index generations of a source

post.description:
The generation is never retrievable again. Invalidating the generation that serves leaves the source without one
until a rebuild activates a replacement, so searches over it return nothing in the meantime. Needs the operator
action `manage_sources`. Mounted only when the deployment provides the indexing service. The body is empty or
`{}`.

200.description: The generation as it now stands.

post.description:
Builds a replacement for the source's index generation from the source itself. The generation that serves keeps
serving until the replacement has been validated and is activated, so there is never a moment without a serving
generation once one existed (unless it was invalidated meanwhile). Needs the operator action `manage_sources`.
Mounted only when the deployment provides the indexing service. The body is empty or `{}`.

Location.description: The path of the source, where its progress is read.

post.description:
Queues a sync of the source: ingestion scans it again and indexes what changed. Requests that arrive while a
sync is queued or running are the same job. The work is a durable background job; read the source's status to
monitor it. Needs the operator action `manage_sources`. Mounted only when the deployment provides the indexing
service. The body is empty or `{}`.

Location.description: The path of the source, where its progress is read.

post.description:
Opens the session whose id the context token carries, creating it on first sight. The principal,
tenant and workspace are the token's; a later token for the same session must be the same
authenticated context (a session cannot change principal, tenant or workspace). Opening is idempotent,
so the answer is always 200. The body is optional and, when present, is `{}`.

200.description: The session, created on first sight or resumed.

delete.description:
Ends the session. The prepared action it was waiting on is invalidated first (`session_ended`); nothing
is ever committed by ending. Ending twice is the same as ending once.

post.description:
Accepts raw `audio/wav` bytes (PCM signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 16000 Hz only). The server computes
the duration from the PCM payload and never trusts a client duration. Default maximum length is 60 seconds
(operator configurable); the body-size limit is derived from that rate. The response is a DictationTranscript
for the host to place in the chat input so the user can edit it. The transcript is data, never instructions;
AlixAI never submits it as a turn; raw audio is not retained. This route does not use the voice-conversation
WebSocket and does not involve VAD: the user's record and stop are the segmentation (`segment_kind`
`user_recorded`).

Errors use the typed envelope: `unavailable` (no STT), `validation_failed` (wrong Content-Type, malformed
WAV, wrong format, too long, too short or silent), `permission_denied`, `resource_exhausted` (budget), and
the existing egress denial when external STT is refused.

get.description:
A server-sent event stream of the announcements of the token's session. A client learns the id of a turn it
started; it can never learn the id of the notice turn an application event opened for its session, so this
stream carries it: each announcement is `id: <seq>`, `event: state_changed`, `data: <announcement JSON on one
line>`, naming the event and the notice turn. Read the notice with
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}/events` under a fresh token (a failed turn: a `stale` error
event and `done`). The announcement is a hint, never the truth: it is kept in memory only as long as the
notice turn is (a few minutes), bounded and lost with the process, and what is pending is always
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/pending`.

The response starts with a `retry:` hint; idle periods carry `: keep-alive` comments; the stream follows
live announcements until the client disconnects. Retained announcements after the cursor are sent first
(`Last-Event-ID` or `cursor`, the later wins; none is every retained one). Announcements are numbered from a
time-based value (the Unix time in seconds when the session's feed began) and the numbers only increase, so a
cursor older than the feed (one kept from before a restart) replays the feed from its start. A cursor that is
not a sequence number or is ahead of the stream is `400`; a session that already has four open streams is
`429`.

The scope is the verified token's, whole, and the session in the path must be the token's. Context tokens are
single use: every open needs a fresh one, so a browser `EventSource` is not usable under header
authentication; use a fetch-based reader.

schema.description:
A `retry:` line, then `id: <seq>`, `event: state_changed`, `data: <SessionAnnouncement JSON>`
frames.

get.summary: Learn that an application event changed the session

get.description:
What the active goal waits for: a confirmation of a prepared action, an answer to a clarification, or
nothing blocking. `pending` is null when there is no goal. Collected values are not returned, only the
field names and where each came from. The confirmation secret is never part of it.
get.summary: Inspect the structured pending state

post.description:
Exactly one of `text`, `choice_id`, `confirmation` and `reject`. A confirmation is a structured input
from the client UI, `{preparation_id, token}`: the model never reads "yes" as consent, and a text turn
can never confirm anything. A level 3 action cannot be confirmed through the AI path: the turn answers
with a `request_step_up` directive.

The turn runs to completion before anything is sent, so the text of a `token` event has already passed
the response verifier, and the events are published into the stream hub before they are sent: the text of
a `token` event is Markdown sanitised as a whole (raw HTML, images and links outside the allowed schemes
removed) and then cut into fragments of at most 4096 characters, so render the concatenated text, not
each fragment alone. The same events, byte for byte, can be read again from
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}/events` after a lost connection. With `Accept: text/event-stream` the events arrive as server-sent events (`id` is
`seq`, `event` is `type`, `data` is the TurnEvent on one line); otherwise as one JSON document. `seq` runs
from 0 without gaps, every event carries the same `turn_id` and the last event is `done`. A turn that
ended in a refusal or a failure has a typed `error` event before `done` (`finish_reason: failed`).

The single-use confirmation secret of a prepared action is not a TurnEvent: it is the
`X-AlixAI-Confirmation-Token` response header of a stream, or `confirmation` in the JSON document. Show it
to the user's client only; present it once, with the preparation id.

A turn that could not be run at all (no valid scope, a limit, a session that is not this context) is an
error response, never a stream. An event the stream refuses (it fails validation) is not sent and not
skipped over: the turn ends with an `error` event and a `done` event with `finish_reason: failed`, at the
next sequence numbers, and the confirmation secret is withheld.

**Attachments.** A text turn may name files the user uploaded (`attachments`, the ids `POST /v1/files`
returned; at most 4). They are resolved together under the turn's scope before anything runs: a reference
that does not resolve for the caller (another tenant's, principal's or session's file, a deleted one, an
expired one, one that never existed) fails the whole turn with one and the same `403 scope_violation` that
says nothing about why, no model is called and no turn is recorded. What a model may see of a file (the
text of a text file, cut to the files configuration's limit and to what the prompt budget has left; never
a path, an id or image bytes) is given to it as untrusted data, in the proposal prompt of that turn only:
it is not the user's message, so it is not routed on, kept in the transcript or shown to a later turn. A
deployment that cannot take attachments in a turn answers `503 unavailable`
(`details.reason` `attachments_unavailable`).

schema.description:
A sequence of `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>`, `data: <TurnEvent JSON>` frames; the `data` of each
validates against schemas/conversation/turn-event.

Event-stream only: the single-use confirmation secret of the action the turn prepared, when it
needs the user's explicit confirmation.

post.summary: Send a turn and receive its events

get.description:
The events of a turn the caller sent, from the turn's replay buffer, so that a client that lost its
connection continues without the turn being run again: this route only reads, and a turn is never
re-run because a client reconnected. The turn is the one `sendTurn` answered for (its `turn_id`, which
every event carries); the buffer keeps a bounded number of events and bytes per turn, and a finished
turn for a few minutes.

**Transport.** Server-sent events by default: each event is `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>` and
`data: <the TurnEvent on one line>`, byte for byte what `sendTurn` sent, followed by a blank line; the
response starts with a `retry:` hint and idle periods carry `: keep-alive` comments, and the stream ends
after the `done` event. A request with `Upgrade: websocket` is served as a WebSocket instead: one text
message per event (the same JSON), server to client only (a message from the client closes the
connection with 1008), the optional subprotocol `alixai.turn-events.v1`, and a normal closure (1000)
after `done`. A browser's `Origin` must be the request's own host: no CORS header is ever sent.

**Resume.** The cursor is the `seq` of the last event the client received, from `Last-Event-ID` or the
`cursor` query parameter (when both are present the later one wins); the stream continues with the next
event, each exactly once and in order. No cursor is the start of the turn. A cursor that is not a
sequence number, or that is ahead of the stream, is `400`; one behind the retained window is `410`
(`expired`, `details.reason: cursor_expired`: the stream is never resumed with a gap, so read the turn's
outcome from the session and the actions API instead); one at the end of a finished turn is `204` (stop
reconnecting). A connection cut off for reading too slowly is closed after a comment (SSE) or with
close code 1013 (WebSocket): reconnect with the last cursor.

**Identity.** The turn is looked up in the caller's whole scope (application, tenant, workspace,
principal and session, all from the token). A turn that does not exist, a turn of another principal and
a turn past its retention are the same `403` (`scope_violation`, `details.reason: turn_not_visible`), so
a turn id is no oracle. A context token is single use, so **every reconnect needs a fresh token**: a
browser `EventSource`, which reconnects by itself and cannot set the `Authorization` header, is not
usable here; read the stream with a fetch-based reader (the SDK's) and mint a token per open.

The single-use confirmation secret of a prepared action is never in a TurnEvent and is not sent here;
it is the response of the turn that prepared the action, once.

101.description: The connection is upgraded to a WebSocket (the request carried `Upgrade: websocket`).

schema.description:
A `retry:` line, then `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>`, `data: <TurnEvent JSON>` frames; the
`data` of each validates against schemas/conversation/turn-event.

200.description: The events of the turn after the cursor.

204.description: The cursor is at the end of a finished turn: the client has every event. Stop reconnecting.

410.description:
The cursor is behind the retained window (`expired`, `details.reason: cursor_expired`): the events
after it are no longer kept.

get.summary: Read the events of a turn again, from a cursor

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket (`Upgrade: websocket`) that carries one voice conversation: the client streams audio
or submits a finalised utterance, the core answers with interim and final transcripts, runs the final
transcript as the user's message on the token's session, and sends the verified response as text and,
when speech is available, as audio. Everything that can be refused is refused with an HTTP status before the
upgrade: the token, the session, a quarantined application, and a deployment with no speech recognition
(`503 unavailable`, `details.effect: text_input_only` -- type instead; the text API is unaffected).

**Identity.** The scope is the verified context token, whole, and nothing a message says: no message
carries a tenant, a workspace, a principal, a role or a scope. The token is single use and is presented in
the `Authorization` header of the upgrade request (never in the URL); the connection lives at most as long as the
token (`1001`, reason `credential_expired`) and at most 15 minutes, and a later connection for the same
session takes over the earlier one (`1001`, reason `replaced`). A browser's `Origin` must be the request's
own host: no CORS header is ever sent. A deployment serves at most four voice connections at a time, at
most two of them for one tenant and one for one user, by default (`503 resource_exhausted`, retryable;
`details.limit` is `deployment`, `tenant` or `principal`).

**Messages.** Text messages are JSON: `ClientMessage` from the client, `ServerEvent` from the core (the
schemas of this area; every event the core sends validates against `ServerEvent`). Binary messages are audio,
raw PCM 16-bit little-endian: from the client while a capture is active (in the format `capture.start`
named, at most `max_chunk_bytes` each), from the core between `playback.started` and `playback.done` or
`playback.cancelled` (in the format `playback.started` announced). The first message is `session.started`.

**Audio in.** Stream: `capture.start`, binary audio, `capture.end` (or `capture.cancel`, which discards
everything). Or submit a whole utterance with `audio.submit` (base64, at most 8 MiB of audio). Interim
transcripts (`transcript.interim`) are for display and never reach the pipeline; the final transcript
(`transcript.final`) is visible to the host before the turn runs and then runs as the user's message. A
recogniser that fails part way yields no transcript at all (`capture.cancelled`, reason `stt_failed`): partial
output is never acted on. The language of a capture is a hint to the recogniser and, when the core supports
it, the language of the reply; the language the recogniser reports is only echoed.

**The turn.** `turn.completed` names the turn, so its events (directive, prepared action, confirmation
panel, citations) are the stream of `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}/events`. A turn that
prepared an action that needs confirmation carries the single-use `confirmation` secret for the client's own
confirm control. **Speech never confirms an action:** there is no message that confirms, rejects or
chooses, and a spoken "yes" is only text. The only confirmation is the structured input of
`POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns`, so a booking started by voice is confirmed on the screen, by text,
in the same session. A speaker-recognition hint, when the deployment has that component, is reported beside
the transcript as a hint and changes nothing about the scope or the permissions.

**Correction.** `transcript.correct` replaces the transcript of the latest utterance with the user's text
before anything is confirmed: the corrected text runs as a new message on the same session, the pipeline's
correction rules void the preparation built on the old transcript (`superseded_preparation_id`), and a
correction after a newer utterance is `stale`. A correction can never change a commit: a commit is a receipt.

**Speech.** The response (`response`) is the model's text that passed the response verifier, or the
deterministic template, and the core checks it once more before it is spoken: speech starts only after the
material facts are verified (`speech: queued`), otherwise the text is delivered and `speech` is `skipped`
with the reason. `playback.cancel` stops the speech at once; a new capture or submission does too (barge-in:
`playback.cancelled`, reason `barge_in`), and after `playback.cancelled` no further audio of that playback is
sent. A response that a newer utterance made stale is not spoken at all (`superseded`).

**When a component fails.** The connection stays open and text keeps working: an `error` event carries the
typed error and the degradation `effect` (`text_input_only` for speech recognition, `verified_text_only`
for speech synthesis, `manual_turn_taking` when no voice-activity detection exists: the client ends each
capture itself). The language pack the connection runs on is taken from the deployment; when it is
deactivated, live captures and playbacks are cancelled (reason `pack_changed`) and the connection stays.

**Privacy.** Raw audio is not retained: the core holds an utterance's audio only while it is recognised,
never writes it to a log, an event or a store, and zeroes it afterwards. A tenant whose policy says so has the
audio of its utterances handed to the deployment's audio store (`retain_raw_audio` in `session.started`);
if it cannot be stored the utterance is dropped (`capture.cancelled`, reason `retention_failed`).

**Close codes.** `1000` the client closed; `1001` the credential expired, the connection was replaced or the
service is stopping; `1008` too many malformed messages; `1009` a message over `max_audio_bytes` once encoded.

get.description:
Exactly the capabilities the policy gateway exposes to this token (the same exposure the model gets), each with
its effective risk level, what a commit needs and what settings do to it: `enabled` is false when any level
switched it off (`disabled_by` names the levels), and `extra_confirmation` marks a confirmation that is required
only because settings asked for it. Settings can switch off and add confirmation; they never add a capability or
lower a requirement. `settings_access` says which settings operations the token permits. The token must carry
`settings.user.read`.
get.summary: The capabilities enabled for the caller

get.description:
The top of the cascade for every tenant and user of the token's application. The deployment level is per
application: a token for application A can never read what application B has (ADR 0016). The token must carry
`settings.deployment.read`.
get.summary: Read the settings of the caller's application as a whole

put.description:
As for the user settings, with the capability scope `settings.deployment.write`. The deployment level is where
voice, attachments and history export are first allowed. What the operator controls for the whole installation
(approved profiles, ceilings, the runtime, external mode, data egress, credentials, budgets, the decision layer)
is configuration and operator-only API and is not a member of this document. The change is recorded on the
application's audit chain.

200.description: The stored document and its new revision.

put.summary: Replace the settings of the caller's application as a whole

get.description:
The deployment, tenant and user settings combined with fixed rules (never a model): preferences take the most
specific level that states them; a permission that enables a feature is the deployment's and every level below
can only switch it off; retention and attachment size are the smallest value any level states, capped by the
operator's ceiling; switched-off capabilities add up; extra confirmation takes the lowest threshold.
`decided_by` names the level that decided each value more than one level can state. The view is read only and is
never an input to the policy gateway. The token must carry `settings.user.read`; the tenant and deployment
documents themselves are not revealed.
get.summary: What the three levels add up to for the caller

get.description:
The findings of the latest integration audit of the installed package, with the remediation status of each
(`open`, `accepted`, `informational`). It is read only: nothing here accepts a warning, activates a package or
changes what the application may do. It answers while the application is quarantined, which is when the findings
matter most. The token must carry `settings.deployment.read`. 503 when this deployment has no audit read-out.
get.summary: The latest integration audit of the caller's application

get.description:
The profiles the operator approved (the `settings.approved_profiles` configuration), the one in force when no
level states one (`default`) and the one the caller's effective settings select (`selected`). A setting selects
among these; it can neither add one nor name an address. The token must carry `settings.user.read`.
get.summary: List the approved model and resource profiles

get.description:
Role, status and stable degradation effect of each model role (controller, router, embedder, reranker, ...).
Nothing about what runs behind a role: no runtime name, address, version or free-text reason. LocalAI's own
endpoints are never exposed. The token must carry `settings.deployment.read`.
get.summary: The health of the model roles

get.description: Defaults and policy for every user of the token's tenant. The token must carry `settings.tenant.read`.
get.summary: Read the settings of the caller's tenant

put.description:
As for the user settings, with the capability scope `settings.tenant.write`. Tenant policy only narrows what
the deployment level allows: voice, attachments and history export are off until the deployment level allows
them; retention and attachment size are ceilings; capabilities switched off here are off for every user of the
tenant; extra confirmation takes the lowest threshold.

200.description: The stored document and its new revision.

put.summary: Replace the settings of the caller's tenant

get.description:
The preferences of the token's principal in the token's workspace. The token must carry the capability scope
`settings.user.read`. A level with no document yet answers version 0 and the empty document, which a first write
expects. An application whose package is not active answers `quarantined`.
get.summary: Read the caller's own user settings

put.description:
Replaces the whole document (a member left out means inherit). The token must carry `settings.user.write`. The
write succeeds only when `expected_version` is still the stored version (0 to create): otherwise 409 `conflict`
with `details.current_version` and nothing changes. The new revision is exactly one more. A document identical to
the stored one changes nothing and is not recorded. Every change is an audit event appended in the same
transaction (`settings.document_written`: level, revisions, changed sections and a digest, never a value).
Capabilities named in `capabilities.disabled` must be ones the caller may itself use: an undeclared, admin-only or
out-of-scope capability is refused with the same 422 `unknown_capability`.

200.description: The stored document and its new revision.

put.summary: Replace the caller's own user settings
